summary.whatChanges: Reworks the type-level normalizer behind `z.toZod<T>()`: intersections are now flattened (so `.and()` and `.safeExtend()` schemas match either spelling of the target) and callables stop the recursion so function signatures survive. Docs for `toZod` move from the basics page to the API page, dropping the intersection caveat.
behaviorChanges: `z.toZod<{a:number}&{b:string}>()` now accepts a `.safeExtend()` schema, and a flat object target now accepts an `.and()` schema; both previously failed to compile
Function-typed targets (e.g. `z.toZod<() => string>()`) are compared by signature instead of being normalized away
The previous requirement that a target equal its own homomorphic rebuild before recursing is removed, changing which nested types get normalized
The `toZod` documentation section is now on the API reference page instead of Basic usage, and the intersection/`Flatten` guidance is gone
risks: Dropping the `AssertEqual<T, {[K in keyof T]: T[K]}>` guard means non-plain object types (arrays, tuples, Date, Promise, class instances, branded types) are now walked and rebuilt, potentially weakening the exactness guarantee or erasing nominality
Unconditional recursion through object properties may increase type instantiation depth and compile time, or hit 'type instantiation is excessively deep' on recursive types
Code relying on the previously-failing intersection vs. flat-object distinction (e.g. tests with `@ts-expect-error`) will now report unused expect-error
Docs no longer mention the `Flatten` workaround, which may leave users of older versions without guidance
